lessons.title: Four Downs

steps.title: Downs
steps.body: The offense gets 4 tries, called downs, to move the ball 10 yards forward.

steps.title: First down!
steps.body: If the offense moves 10 yards, that is a first down! They get 4 brand new tries.

steps.title: Punt
steps.body: On 4th down, teams often punt. They kick the ball far away so the other team starts farther from their end zone.

steps.prompt: How many yards must the offense move to earn a first down?
steps.explanation: Ten yards earns a new set of downs.

steps.prompt: How many tries (downs) does the offense get?

steps.statement: When a team gets a first down, it gets 4 new tries.
steps.explanation: Yes! That is why first downs are so important.
Downs go 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th. Then the other team gets the ball unless you made a first down.

steps.prompt: It is 4th down and 15 yards to go, far from the end zone. What should the coach do?

options.why: Punting sends the ball far away so the other team has a long way to go.
15 yards is very hard. If you miss, the other team starts close to your end zone.
The goal posts are way too far away.

steps.explanation: When it is 4th down and a long way to go, punting is the safe, smart choice.

lessons.blurb: Four tries to go ten yards.

lessons.title: Running and Passing

steps.title: The snap
steps.body: The center passes the ball back to the quarterback. This is the snap. The snap starts every play!

steps.title: Handoff
steps.body: In a handoff, the quarterback hands the ball to a running back. The running back runs with it.

steps.title: Pass
steps.body: In a pass, the quarterback throws the ball to a receiver. If nobody catches it, it is an incomplete pass and the play is over.

steps.title: Tackle
steps.body: The defense stops a runner by tackling: bringing them to the ground. In flag football, they pull a flag instead.

steps.prompt: What is it called when the QB hands the ball to a runner?
steps.explanation: The QB hands off the ball to a running back.

steps.statement: If a pass hits the ground, the play is over.
steps.explanation: That is an incomplete pass. The ball goes back and the team tries again.

steps.prompt: Match the word to what it means.

pairs.right: QB gives the ball to a runner

steps.explanation: These four words are used on almost every play.

steps.prompt: How do you stop the ball carrier in tackle football?
steps.explanation: Yes. In tackle football the play ends when the runner is tackled. In flag football you pull a flag.

lessons.blurb: Two ways to move the ball.

steps.title: Turnover
steps.body: A turnover is when the defense takes the ball away from the offense. The ball changes teams right away!

steps.title: Interception
steps.body: An interception is when a defender catches the quarterback's pass. The defense now has the ball!

steps.title: Fumble
steps.body: A fumble is when the runner drops the ball. Anyone can pounce on it. Whoever recovers it gets the ball.

steps.prompt: A defender catches the quarterback's pass. What is that called?
A runner drops the ball and the other team grabs it. What happened?
steps.explanation: The runner fumbled, and the other team recovered it.

steps.statement: After a turnover, the other team gets the ball.
steps.explanation: That is what makes turnovers so big.
